column1: # What counts as the CSP meta (Replikanti/interviewscam#32): a meta whose
# http-equiv is an ASCII case-insensitive match for Content-Security-Policy,
# untrimmed, as the browser matches the keyword (is_csp_meta in
# tools/sitecheck.py), read with HTML's tokenizer (csp_metas). One row per reader of the CSP meta and per padding
# member (a leading or trailing space, a tab, a newline, U+00A0 and the
# non-ASCII guard U+017F, the long s that casefold and NFKC fold to s), plus
# the case variants, a valueless and a duplicate http-equiv, a non-meta
# element at the CSP position and a padded refresh. A padded value is inert
# in the browser, so it must not count: only/<member> (the count), first/
# (the position) fail, and intake/ (site rule (a)) and policy/ (the CSP
# rules) stay silent about it. On a copy of render/pass-intake (the real
# built pages, no built pins, so rule (m) does not hide a row) through
# site_intake_runner in tools/selftest.sh, label site-csp-equiv. Columns:
# name, file, find, replace, expect (PASS; PASS-OR-ONLY <text>, a pass or
# findings that all hold <text>; or a text the findings must hold), then
# optional further find and replace pairs. \n and \t in find and
# replace are a newline and a tab, \u{XXXX} that code point, so the
# table holds only ASCII; U+00A0 and U+017F go into the attribute rows raw,
# not as character references, because the CSP rules read the raw value
# with HTML's tokenizer and refuse every '&' there
# write a raw code point into tag markup. Outside a quoted value site rule
# (i) fails it before any parser's reading matters, so the verdict is the
# same on every html.parser: per member of PARSER_ONLY_SPACE one row in the
# CSP meta's unquoted http-equiv value (tag-space/uXXXX) and one after its
# quoted value, between the attributes (tag-space/after-quoted/uXXXX); and
# rows in the tag name, before and after '=', in an unquoted value that
# holds a quote, after a quoted '>', after two '>' in one quoted value (a
# reader that left the quotes at the first would end the tag at the
# second), in an end tag and in the DOCTYPE; after a bogus comment ('</'
# and a non-letter, fix round 2) holding a quote, and after a quote or
# '/="' in an attribute name, which open no value. Inside a quoted value both
# parsers read the same text, so those rows pass (U+00A0 double- and
# single-quoted, and U+000B, U+0085, U+2028, U+3000), as do TAB, LF, FF and
# CR between the attributes and U+00A0 in text.
